If you love story driven games then give this a try. Can be somewhat slow at times and you can tend to get lost which is a good and bad thing. Sometimes you find really awesome things lurking behind that bush that can offer peices to a much larger story or beautiful landscape views other times it's just a dead end (which happens a lot more than you'd like to admit) Really great story all the way through. Great game don't expect to be playing for long I beat it in about 4 hours. Not too much replayability but a good experience none-the-less

I honestly thought this game was something horror-related; I was skeptical throughout the first part. I don't know, I just randomly bought this game under Winter Sale and called it a day. It was damn worth my few last dollars in my Wallet.

(Delilah is a baddie)
Good story, amazing writing, very relaxing and simple to play. One of my favorite games of all time, loved it!

This game has provoked entirely too much introspection for my comfort.

Rated 'M' for married/middle-aged audiences.

To persons put off by the "Walking Simulator" school of games: it's really more of a Talking Simulator, instead. Yes, you traipse across the Shoshone, but the essence and development of the game lies in the conversations that you have with your fellow lookouts.

A lovely atmospheric game with gorgeous visuals, pacing, music and voice acting. Tense and self-reflective, I enjoyed every moment of it from beginning to end. I can't recommend it enough, although this is no Hideki Kamiya game - the gameplay is second seat for the player. It can be slow and quiet at points, just like nature.

I fucking hate going outside - and I hate the summer. But this game made me want to lie in a national park and consider how to unfuck my life.

I love the entire premise of this game, which touches on some very dark and depressing topics that haunt all characters involved. The dialogue and voice acting is great, and it really makes me want to meet Delilah in person and go for drinks!
There's just the right amount of humourous options to pick through in the dialogue to lighten the mood of what would otherwise be a really gutwreching summer for Henry.
This is the type of game that really makes one wonder how they would respond in a similar situation, and I have to say I would've handled it far worse.
It's very soothing walking among the nicely rendered wilderness - nothing too over the top, but the slight pastel colour pallette also helps to offset how heavy this subject matter is. The countryside reminds me a lot of the Long Dark, which is another favorite so I might be a little biased...in any case, I highly recommend this game, though I do wish it was longer over all.

Very enjoyable. Extremely random that me and a friend picked this game up tbh, but it was like $2 aud so I just went for it. Was definitely worth it. Very mature, good writing. You can slightly see and feel the "2016 indie game" energy in it but honestly doesn't affect it much. I want more games like this. Ykno, games that are somewhat nature focused but aren't just annoying walking simulators with no gameplay substance. This one tackles some pretty heavy stuff tho, even if it's not going for pure shock value.

This is a nice short game with a powerful story. The story gives a few strong messages. The graphics are cool and really stylized. The scenery is very beautiful. The dialogue is well written and the comedy in this game is good. The walkie talkie friendship that develops over the course of the game is great and stood out. Only took me 4 hours to play through the whole game so if you like replay ability then don't get this. I do recommend it but only when it is on sale for half off or more. $20 is a little much for only 4 hours of play.
Beautiful game! This is my third time playing it, but instead it's on my own account. Definitely get it if you like word play and a simple story.

Finished this linear story in one sitting but it was quite a compelling one as you want to know the outcome! A psychological mystery although you never knew if it was going to turn into a horror story and that air of suspense is always a sign of a good game. Graphics were fairly low-res but this didn't subtract from the exploration enjoyment. Excellent non-cheesy voice acting too.

Great game with some great VA's for great(er) roles. The two main characters in this game carry so much depth to them - and with your character, you can slightly alternate his personality and / or attitude towards things via different response options. Watching the irony of the situation in the story unfold nearer to the end is one of the greatest parts about this game imo - a lot of the tension is carried in the characters conspiracies and / or exaggerated thoughts, and when it comes together into the actual reality, its almost harrowing in comparison.
This is not another walking simulator. This is a great enjoyable game, the plot and the atmosphere are awesome, and this 5-6 hours experience will stick with you for a while.

Wow. Just wow. 5 minutes into the game I felt horribly sorry for the dude. Then the end, this guy just ain't got any luck. Amazing game. I don't even normally like games where they are more mystery oriented and less the action type. But I started playing this game and couldnt stop. Took me abour 3-4 horus to beat it, but it was definitely worth the 10 dollars I paid on humble bundle to get it.

10/10 - would hear a horribly depressing story again.

Firewatch is excellent. An amazing, albeit short adventure. Even though it's merely a walking simulator, it has a very compelling story with well developed characters that had me hooked throughout the entire game. The dialogue is a very important element in the game and it was very well made in terms of creativity with excellent voice acting. The world is beautiful, drawn in a minimalistic style with a lovely atmosphere. It was very immersive - it really felt as if I was actually wandering through the wilderness of Wyoming. Truly a memorable experience.
This is one of my favorite games. It's one that I highly recommend, and it is best to just dive in without seeing ant traillers or gameplay. Enjoy it; you won't regret purchasing this game.
Great story telling. Beautiful game in visuals and in emotions. I loved it and will come back to replay it later.

[original review] Super cool game! Very adicting, fun but also a little creepy sometimes!!

It has been close to six years since I wrote my initial review shown above and I still can't find the right words to describe how amazing this game is. The graphics, music, story telling, it all fits together extremely well.

I remember discovering this game in 2018 when I was looking for Premiere Pro tutorials on how to end a song with an echo effect. I stumbled upon a random video where some dude showed me exactly how to achieve the results I was aiming for, using clips from the trailer. I was hooked instantly by the music and visual style.

I've finished 3 full playthroughs so far and can't wait to play it again. In my eyes it truly is the best adventure game that has ever been published.

As many of you may know, Santo Campo has been acquired by Valve and put a hold on their latest project "In the Valley of the Gods". Even though it says the game is planned to release December 2029, I'm afraid it never will.

Nontheless, I thank everyone who has helped bring this game to life.

Decent game, but it was only about 4 hours of content if you take your time. I wish there was more, but it's a very enteraining story that draws you in fast and next thing you know the game is over. Neat, but leaves you wanting more.

Didn't mind contributing to the devs with the cost, as I hope the keep building similiar titles and keep up their good work.
Firewatch is less a video game and more a profound meditation on the human condition. A Experience, A journey which you should not miss. 10/10

I was enamored. I've always enjoyed short story games such as this. Definitely on my top 5 list of favorite story genres. Captivates you from start to finish and you can adopt a pet turtle. 10/10

People that say it has a bad ending are just mad because the developers had the balls to produce an ending game of thrones couldn't.

The whole game is simply enjoyable to look at, it's clear that the designers spent a lot of time carefully designing the paths and nature around the paths that you have to navigate as you progress through the game. I really have only one complaint, there's one unresolved plot point near the end of the game that was irritating to have left open-ended. Besides that it's anti-climatic to not ever get the chance to meet Delilah, whom you've spent the whole game talking to. So much build up to never get the chance to see her.

Overall, I highly recommend the game. It really is excellent and enjoyable to play, just don't expect your decisions to matter too much, you can choose to do and say any of the options and get the same ending.

The first part of the game is kinda boring with the dialog stopping you in the adventure, but god damn it's getting better. Only 4 hours to finish the game but TOTALLY worth it, Story is very nice like the graphics. Another master piece.

A middle aged man's, Henry, emotional catharsis by walking around in the woods. Surely it impacts you more if you've experienced the loss of a loved one. A story driven game that makes you think at the end: should we move on from that love or try harder to fix things? I think it ended pretty beautifully calling out escapism

Firewatch is not a game for everyone, but more like a good book. Over the course of its 4 hour campaign i was always excited about what would happen next. It builds up a story wich is confusing but in the end makes sense. Great characters, exciting story but a suprising ending. 9/10

It's a peaceful and relaxing game with a gripping story that results in a dramatic twist. All of this goes hand in hand with beautiful sights and a perfectly fitting ambient soundtrack making Firewatch one of the best narrative games ever made.

If you got hooked on games like Life is Strange, Journey, or The Wolf Among Us, this is the ideal pick for you.

It’s very hard to talk about games like this, that are all about the story, without spoilers but I will give it a shot.

The game manages to make you emotionally involved from the start. It does a very good job of weaving a story that keeps you curious but also a bit tense. The game mechanics are simple and this is fine in this context. The accent is on atmosphere but without it being (too) scary or horror, so if you’re a scary cat like me this game will be just perfect. The art style is excellent and really helps in creating that perfect atmosphere.

Firewatch takes around 4-5 hours for most people, and for me it was most definitely an experience that I enjoyed having, and I will remember it fondly as a game done right.

Firewatch is simply one of the best "walking simulator" out there in the market, and the only "forest ranger simulator". So, sure, we all heard the ridiculous "play fast and refund" stories that a fair amount of disrespectful dudes spread, and the game is kinda short, true, but in my opinion, 4 hours is a pretty decent game time for this particular type of narrative experience... long enough to feel satisfied, but also short enough not to get bored!

So, the art is simple, kind of cartoonish, but it's nice, also, there are loads of details and minor easter eggs, and the voice acting is very convincing (it's very easy to get attached to both the main character and her radio contact). And last but not least, the story is really good, not predictable at all, emotional, but never cheesy.

So if you're into first person narrative games, get Firewatch, it really is a great game!
A relaxing, fast-paced, and deep adventure that stays with you after you finish it and makes you want to play it again.

This is a game I wasn’t sure buying, and after playing it I can tell you that I don’t regret it.
I thought the game was just chill, but after launching it for the first time, I didn’t close it until I had finished it (4.5h non-stop).
In this “choice making” game, all that matters is your perception of the environment, because in this beautiful forest (incredible graphism that run on a low end pc) there is a fear that someone is watching you, you haven’t seen anyone but the fear mixed with the beauty of the game, build a tension.The game start on a simple but effective gameplay that put you into the story without having any contact with another person and you’re only contact with someone will be with your colleague delilah (super fun girl).
I won’t tell u more things about the game (except to buy it), so go ahead.
Absolutely loved this game, the tension and suspense was perfect. Loved the music while just walking through the forest in certain scenes. Loved the story, couldn't of guessed it. 10/10

So going into this, I thought that this was a Firewatch Simulator game with a bit of a character development and some "mysterious" backstory. My plan was to check it out and to see if it'll be cool to play on my Steamdeck. I got immediately hooked and played through the game in two sessions in a span of two days.

Now that I've played through it, I'm stunned, like Holy Sh*t ! What a good Story. The Intro itself even touched me and made me tear up a bit. This Game made me laugh, sad, scared as shit and feel amazed. I really liked that you can choose your own adventure with what to say via the Radio. Once I've realized that you have to unravel this whole Mystery, I thought that it would require a second play through, but I appreciate that the game makes you to not forget or miss doing things. The only thing I didn't like is that Henry and Delilah didn't get to meet in person at the end. A big hug between the two would've made the End into a Happy End for me.

For me this is one of those Games where going into it, I didn't expect much but in the end I'm very happy that I've played it through.

Hands down, the graphics are just absolutely beautiful. The storytelling itself starts off really good as well with great intentions and energy.
However the further you get into the game the more it loses that momentum. It feels more and more as a linear track narrative that you just walk down. Until you come to the end which felt completely out of my control and very disappointing for a narrative game.

So while there was a lot of potential in the story, graphics and gameplay, it loses so much energy and narrative influence from the player towards the end that I think a lot of people will be really disappointed.
I would give it a 3.5/5 if I wouldn't be faced with a binary choice.

Firewatch is a... curious game. It's a story-driven ambiance exploration title (aka. "walking simulator") with a both simple and complex premise. The playable character's life is in a tough spot, so he seeks escape to rethink it and decides to work for one summer as a fire lookout in the wilderness. And most of the game is mostly about having conversations about everyday tough choices with the partner's voice over the radio. With the more or less open map and some optional exploration being just a backdrop to the story, something to go along the idea of escaping the situation you are in via incredible adventuring, but never really going that far from it.

And the game is great at it. It always tries to hook you up with promise of something exciting, while keeping things grounded and, in the end, might very much manage to surprise you with mundane. Yet, that is also one of the reasons I couldn't help but feel slightly disappointed with it while playing, since it never felt truly going anywhere. As is, it's a great story-driven game that's worth checking out. But don't expect it to be more than what it is after the opening minutes. Unless you try to make it be so, which, I suppose, was also intentional.

The story is fucking amazing, only complaint is it can be short, as I beat it in 3 hours, taking my time as well. The ending was phenomenal and left me emotionally feeling it for hours, as the story builds up great connections with all characters involved. Overall, 10/10 game.

Firewatch is a game I can only recommend for the visuals and banter between the two main characters because aside from that, the game offers very little else.

The story has lots of promise and even has a few moments of tension but the payoff is always lacklustre and trust me when I say the events you conjure in your mind about what will happen next are definitely better than what actually does.

While the dialogue between the characters plays out in a sort of, your answer matters way, trust that it doesn't, you can go through this game with very little communication and the response is always the same as if you did say something, there is no comment from the other character if you fail to answer properly as she will just take the reins and push the story onward anyways.

The option to free roam after finishing the game is a nice touch but I'm pretty sure, with the gear acquired, you can travel anywhere, for how ever long you want during the story anyway, free roam just eliminates the objective and option to banter.

This is also a fairly short game too. I did the story and got all ten achievements in under four hours, so if you are curious about this game, then definitely wait till it is on sale.

I played this game a while back on my Switch and I really enjoyed it. I saw this game was on sale a few months ago and decided to buy it again for my PC. I just finished the game not to long ago and had forgotten how good this game was! I really liked the adventure style of this game. The graphics are stunning (in my opinion). This game isn't to long, it only took me about 3 hours to beat the game with all of the achievements. If you enjoy a good adventure game, then please do play this one, it does not disappoint!

Such an enjoyable game. I held off from buying this but the STEAM sale this holiday season finally gave me the excuse to take the plunge.

If you are looking for action, then you should probably take a pass on this, but if you are into exploring a vibrant, interesting environment in the vein of Dear Esther, The Vanishing of Ethan Carter or Gone Home, then you should already own this.

There is a greater sense of engagement than most walking simulators. The narrative strikes a nice middle ground between the ambiguity of Dear Esther and the investivative feel of The Vanishing of Ethan Carter. There is no face-to-face time, but the characters are engaging- particularly Delilah.

One of the unexpected treats for me was the audio commentary tour of the game after my first playthrough. I love that they added the little detail of having commentary delivered via cassette tapes scattered around the map.

I feel a little guilty that I didn't support the developers through a full-priced purchase but I'm very happy that I finally took the plunge. Thank you, Campo Santo.

Simple yet great graphics, quite easy game play, and simple yet catchy story line. To a point it is like a choose your own adventure with responses to dialog, but I am not sure how much it actually effects the overall outcome of the game. This game is somewhat short, but if you like adventure games, this game is definitely worth a must. I finished the game in about 5 hours, but I always like enjoying the scenery, so you might finish sooner.

Captivating story, teaming with mystery and suspense. Visually stunning for an indie-type game. Bear in mind it is a very slow paced game, making it different to a lot of the 'go go go' type games that flood the market of late. The game is short and re-play ability is limited. However, it is thought provoking and I give it a 10/10 for what it is trying to achieve.

I enjoyed it. The story pulled me in and I wanted to learn what was going on. I liked how I could basically explore what I wanted as the game progressed. I was about to beat in about 3 hours but could have spent another hour or so exploring if I had wanted to. It's worth a look when it's on sale if you play games for the story.
One of the Indie classic adventure. A good 5-7 hours story and gameplay, buy it on SALE.

I'm not sure how much decisions mattered in this game. Maybe different choices give a slightly different story. Narration was on point, and there's a lot of it. It's open world but pretty linear in where it guides you. Definately enjoyable in a relaxing sort of way. Wife found ending dissapointing, but it's a story, it wasn't what she wanted it to be, but everything can't be like that, I mean, dammit, girl, so I gained a few pounds, you need to let off the steam a bit. I work out, but I also like to eat. You knew that when you married me! And don't act like this isn't a 2-way street! You need to get off the facebooks all the damn time. I like a little human interaction from time to time too!
This game is incredible. Native gamepad and Linux support, too. I'm not gonna say too much, I personally think this game is a great one to just sit down and play in one go.

This is one beautiful game , in more ways than just graphical , the story's phenomenal, too .
Honestly, it's up there with the fallout franchise (except for the 4th) and the game Life is Strange.
Even the opening screen brings up a great deal of emotion and joy of the experience I had of it , like
a great game should .

I give it a 10/10.
Definitely a must play.
Kraťoulinká hra, ale zanechá ve vás pocit, že chcete víc! Doporučuji ji chytit ve slevě.
This game was a fun walkthrough story, felt interesting enough. Would wait for this game to be on sale.

I have mixed feeling regarding this game.
The start of it did not made much sense to me - I was unsure about the purpose of some things.
After finishing the game, I felt a bit disappointed.

In between I discovered a beautiful world (graphics is kind of unique). Voice acting is superb. I liked Delilah a lot, even though the main character seemed like the most ordinary dude from the US. The experience was nice, however it could have been better. There is some extra content, which rounds up the game as a whole (free roam, developer comments).

7/10

This game, was ABSOLUTE CINEMA. THIS GAME LITERALLY CHANGED MY ENTIRE VIEW ON LIFE. THIS IS A MASTERPIECE. NO TRIPLE A GAME HAS EVER MADE ME FEEL HOW THIS GAME DID. THE VISUALS, PLOT, LORE, STORY, ITS JUST ALL SO BEAUTIFUL. Exploring at night does get a little spooky, but i would 10/10 recommend this to someone.

I normally hate first person narrative games, because there are so many examples that are clunky with poorly designed worlds and pace. But occasionally, you stumble across something that is well refined and special.

Beautiful stylised art.
Walking Simulator, except good.
Exceptional voice acting. Very believable characters.
Expertly written. A good mystery keeps you guessing.
A realistic imagining on what it's like to be a fire lookout. Seeing the world through another's eyes is at the heart of what storytelling is.

reason.text: Negative reviews mostly object to DMCA takedowns against a Let's Play streamer, which reviews say conflicts with the developer's stated permission to stream.
A PC Gamer news report covers a YouTuber's DMCA copyright claim, the same type of takedown these reviews describe.

lines.F2: Sep 2017: 51% positive across 1,872 reviews (920 negative), against a usual 90% positive and 30 negative a month

lines.R11: (negative review, 3h played) "Can you stream it? Developer: Yes. We love that people stream and share their experiences in the game. You are free to monetize your videos as well. Developer: Threatens DMCA of all Firewatch content from a streamer because they didn't like them."
lines.R12: (negative review, 4h played) "It looks pretty but it's a very linear experience with no replay value. Using the DMCA for takedowns despite giving explit permission to make Let's Play videos is an abhorent abuse of the legal system - so I cannot recommend this game or any..."
lines.R15: (negative review, 5h played) "The game is very boring. I did not enjoy it. Developer abusing the the DMCA for personal political beliefs. Can't recommend giving money to anyone like this."

tldr.text: Very Positive (89%): players love the story and characters and the art, but the story and characters also draw the most complaints.
Complaints focus on the story and characters, which some call weak.

details.text: Recent reviews complain about the story and characters far less often than they did before.
Players who have logged under two hours are far less positive, at 65%, than those with more time, at 90%.
